"The gypsy moth is a foreign insect that has become. one of the United States' most important forest pests. A single defoliation cankill some softwood trees; two or more defoliations can kill many types of hardwoods. Gypsy moths became established in this country in 1869, after specimens imported from Europe escaped from a laboratory in Massachusetts. The gypsy moth became a pest becauset country did not have the natural enemies that help keep the pest in check in Europe and Asia. In 1968, gypsy moth infestations were observed for the first time in the Newark, New Jersey watershed. Over the next two summers, nearly 18,000 acres of trees sus- tained repeated 75% to 100% defoliations on nearly all susceptible tree species.
